Subject: Console: condensed route comparison & quick export request

Hi team,

I ran a sync with Acme (ops@acme-analytics.com) yesterday; they asked for an "apples-to-apples" view that lets them pick up to three routes and compare cost/latency distributions side-by-side, plus exportable snapshots (CSV and a pre-signed link) for finance and SRE reviews. They also want an SLA-exception annotation so they can correlate spikes to deploys or fallback events.

I attached a quick wireframe (compare-view-wireframe.png) and a small sample query I used to prototype numbers (sample-query.sql). High-level asks:
- Quick compare: select 1–3 routes, time window, baseline vs candidate overlay
- Distribution view: p50/p90/p99 + cost-per-token histograms
- SLA tags: surface flagged windows where latency or error SLOs were breached
- Snapshot export: CSV + short-lived download link for sharing
- Ability to pin a snapshot and compare a live route vs pinned snapshot

Questions for you:
1) Is this feasible without a platform-wide schema change for route metadata?
2) What sampling/aggregation constraints should we call out in the product copy?
3) Rough effort estimate (backend / frontend) so we can prioritize in the next observability planning meeting.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Wednesday to align on scope and acceptance criteria. If we can get a dev estimate today, I can push this into the sprint planning doc.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Console: condensed route comparison & quick export request

Jasmine — thanks for the clear brief and the wireframe, helpful. Quick technical readout and constraints: 

1) Current state:
- Per-route telemetry is stored as minute-level aggregates with a 30-day raw retention. We also keep sampled token-level traces for 48 hours only.
- Route metadata exists but is sparse: owner and tier are present; we do not currently store SLO definitions or exception labels on routes.

2) Feasibility notes:
- Side-by-side compare: doable by materializing a small precomputed timeseries for each route keyed by (route_id, window_bucket). Querying three precomputed series and rendering client-side is reasonable.
- Distribution histograms (p50/p90/p99): we already compute these nightly for billing slices; exposing near-real-time (minute) percentiles will require either (a) higher-resolution aggregation or (b) on-the-fly approximate algorithms (t-digest). Option (b) may be faster to ship.
- SLA tags: requires a tagging surface. We can implement a separate "slo_events" store that references route_id + time_window + event_reason. That avoids changing route schema but needs a small infra component.

3) Effort estimate (rough):
- Backend: 2 backend engineers, ~2 sprints to add precomputation + slo_events store + export endpoint (CSV + pre-signed S3 links).
- Frontend: 1–2 frontend engineers, ~1 sprint for the UI, charting, and export UX.
- Ops: small DB migration window for precomputed tables; low risk.

Acceptance criteria suggestions:
- Compare view can render 3 routes in <800ms median time for a 1-week window (when using cached precomputed series).
- CSV export includes timestamped p50/p90/p99, tokens, cost estimate per row, and flagged SLA boolean.
- Snapshot links expire after 72 hours and are revocable.

Questions for product:
- Do we need to include token-level cost breakdown per model variant? That increases both backend compute and export size.
- What retention for snapshots do we want by default (72h vs 30d)? 72h is simplest operationally.

Happy to scope in the sync.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Observability Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference

Love the wireframe — a few design notes from a prototyping POV: 

- Layout: put the timeline scrubber above charts so users can lock to a spike. When a scrub is pinned, allow side-by-side with live.
- Export modal: default to CSV but give a "presentation snapshot" that generates a PNG of the current view (useful for exec decks).
- SLA annotation: show inline colored badges on the timeline with hover detail (deploy id, error class). We should allow users to add short notes to snapshot exports.

I created a quick prototype in Figma (link below) that shows the pinned snapshot workflow and export modal. If product is happy, I can knock out a clickable prototype for user testing next week.

Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/compare-view-prototype

Thanks for the quick follow-up. A few clarifications from Acme's side: 
- CSV is critical. Please include a tokens column and a model_variant column if available.
- Pre-signed link for snapshot is preferred (72h expiry is fine).
- If possible, include a small metadata section in the CSV with the pinned snapshot notes and SLO tag IDs.

We'd be happy to be beta users and provide a short list of routes to validate.

Subject: Decision: move condensed compare into obs sprint 18 (split backend/frontend)

Thanks everyone — alignment notes and plan:

1) Scope: ship core compare view (3-route overlay, p50/p90/p99, CSV export with tokens + model_variant if present, SLA tags surfaced) as MVP. PNG presentation snapshot is deferred to phase 2.
2) Timeline: allocate to Observability sprint 18 (backend tickets: OBS-743, OBS-744; frontend ticket: OBS-745). Backend work first sprint, frontend second sprint (parallelize where possible).
3) Acceptance criteria: follow Dylan's suggestions; add: export CSV must include snapshot metadata and SLO tag IDs.
4) Beta: Acme agreed to be early testers; Sam will share 6 routes by end of next week.

Action items:
- Dylan: create backend RFC + initial ticket estimates by EOD Friday (OBS-743/OBS-744).
- Marissa: prototype clickable Figma and handoff tokens for charting libs (due next Tue).
- Marcus: add RBAC check for export endpoints (security sign-off).
- Jasmine: schedule 30m kickoff Tuesday 10am PT and update sprint tracker.

I'll keep Acme in the loop and open the Jira tickets. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
